prompts.prompt: hld.md (approved) and stories.md describe the expense reporting app. I have 4 engineers: Dana (has built Step Functions workflows before), Eli, Farah and Gus. Split the work into independent features so each engineer can work in parallel without waiting on the others, and tell me what has to be agreed up front. Write feature-split.md. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in the file, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill prescribes a specific Feature Split format (Scope, User Stories, Key Components, Dependencies, Engineer per feature, plus a Shared Interfaces section to define first) and splitting by data ownership so no two features write the same entity without a shared interface. A competent plan without it often splits by layer or by screen, leaves the Report status written by several features, and never names the report-submitted event as the contract.

floor_checks.text: Uses the Feature Split format: '# Feature Split:' title and '## Feature N:' sections
floor_checks.check: grep -qE '^# Feature Split' feature-split.md && [ $(grep -cE '^## Feature [0-9]+' feature-split.md) -ge 3 ]

floor_checks.text: Every user story US-1..US-9 is mapped
floor_checks.check: for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9; do grep -qE "US-$i\b" feature-split.md || exit 1; done

rubric.pass: '# Feature Split:' title, '## Feature N:' sections each with Scope, User Stories, Key Components, Dependencies, Engineer, and a '## Shared Interfaces' section stating what to define first
rubric.partial: Format mostly followed but one field missing in several features, or Shared Interfaces missing

rubric.criterion: Boundaries by domain / data ownership (KEY tracks)
rubric.pass: Features align to expense API+client, receipt/OCR, approval workflow + notifications + escalation, policy engine, reimbursement export (merging small ones sensibly for 4 people); each entity has one writing feature or a named shared interface
rubric.partial: Reasonable features but one entity (usually Report status) written by two features with no shared contract
rubric.fail: Split by layer or by screen, or heavy overlap

rubric.pass: Names the Report/LineItem schema and the report-submitted event (and the policy evaluation contract) as shared, with which features use each
rubric.partial: Names the schema but not the event, or vice versa
rubric.fail: No shared interfaces, or generic 'agree on APIs'

rubric.pass: No circular dependencies, no feature requires another to be finished to start (stubs/contracts used), all US-1..US-9 mapped, Dana assigned the Step Functions track, sizes plausible for one engineer
rubric.partial: One gate item violated (e.g. export blocked until approval is finished)
rubric.fail: Circular or blocking dependencies, or stories missing

rubric.pass: No new components or stories invented; assumptions listed
rubric.fail: New scope presented as part of the design

prompts.prompt: break down the expense reporting app (hld.md, stories.md) into implementation tasks for the team so we can start planning sprint 1. write it to breakdown.md. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in the file, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill states that 'break down X into implementation tasks' means its Feature Split, not a layer-by-layer technical breakdown (Data Model -> Backend -> API -> Frontend -> Cross-cutting). A competent model without the skill almost always produces the layered list, which creates hand-offs between people instead of independent tracks.

floor_checks.text: Top-level sections are not technical layers (Data Model / Backend / API / Frontend)
floor_checks.check: test -s breakdown.md && ! grep -qiE '^##? *(phase [0-9]+:? *)?(data model|backend|api( contract)?|frontend|cross[- ]cutting)\s*$' breakdown.md

rubric.criterion: Chooses the feature-split shape over a layered breakdown
rubric.pass: Engineer-scoped features with story mapping and a Shared Interfaces section; any task lists sit inside features
rubric.partial: Features present but a parallel layered section drives the plan

rubric.pass: Explains how features can start in parallel (agreed schema/event contracts, stubs) and avoids features that block each other
rubric.partial: Some features blocked on others without a contract

rubric.pass: Suggests what to do first (shared interfaces / foundation) and an order, with rough effort per feature
No generic tasks unrelated to the HLD (e.g. 'set up Kubernetes', 'write documentation') presented as features

prompts.prompt: Plans changed: only 2 engineers and 6 weeks for the expense reporting app (hld.md, stories.md). Split it into features, give each an effort estimate, flag anything too big or too small for one engineer, and propose an implementation order. Write split-2eng.md. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in the file, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate sets size bounds (over 2 weeks: split; under 2 days: merge), asks for a foundation feature that defines shared interfaces, and forbids blocking dependencies. With two engineers a strong answer regroups the five tracks into right-sized features and checks the total against 12 engineer-weeks; a competent answer without the skill tends to list features with estimates but no size flags and no capacity check.

rubric.pass: Each feature estimated; any >2 weeks is split and any <2 days merged (e.g. export or notifications merged into a neighbor), with the reason stated
rubric.partial: Estimates present but size flags missing or inconsistent with the bounds

rubric.pass: Total effort compared to 2 engineers x 6 weeks; order starts with a foundation/shared-interfaces feature and keeps both engineers busy in parallel; names what to cut or defer if over capacity
rubric.partial: Order given but no capacity check, or capacity check but no parallel plan

rubric.pass: Features keep Scope, User Stories, Key Components, Dependencies, Engineer; Shared Interfaces section; all US-1..US-9 mapped
Estimates stated as assumptions with basis; no false precision
rubric.fail: Implausible estimates (e.g. whole app in 1 week)
